answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power in proportion to tokens locked for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents leaves their combined voting power at 100 tokens, so each identity is no island of fresh influence. Even a whisper campaign needs real capital to gain weight. The rule is crystal clear: to control a vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize enough tokens to outweigh honest participants, bearing both the purchase cost and a month of lost liquidity.
